quotes.text: it's failing for one reason. Not the tools, the model behind it. Policies built to block lose to policies built to guide.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core thesis in a memorable contrast.

quotes.text: A credit card number in an email to a payment processor is business. The same number in an email to a personal address is a problem.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows concretely why content patterns alone cannot judge risk.

quotes.text: Here's the asymmetry. Trust erodes faster than risk falls. A policy can take months to reduce real exposure. It takes about a week to lose the people it depends on.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why aggressive blocking backfires on DLP programs.

quotes.text: Justification isn't friction, it's data. Every time someone overrides, they hand you a small piece of information you couldn't get any other way.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes user overrides as tuning input instead of a loophole.

quotes.text: Every false positive is a policy defect. The threshold was too low, the scope was too wide. The pattern was too loose. The exception was missing.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Puts responsibility for noise on policy design, not users.

takeaways: DLP policies built to block drive users to invisible workarounds, so design policies that use context and guide people with tips before enforcing.
Run every policy in simulation for weeks, then with tips but no enforcement, and block only high-confidence, high-volume risks with a reporting path.
Treat DLP as an ongoing practice with a named owner, weekly tuning from overrides and triage, owned and expiring exceptions, and metrics like true positive rate instead of block counts.
hook: A new DLP policy blocks everything on Monday, and by Friday half the finance team is mailing files from personal accounts. This episode is for Microsoft 365 admins and compliance owners who want Purview DLP policies people actually accept. You'll learn how to detect the right data, guide users with tips and overrides, test safely, triage alerts and measure what really works.
